findings.summary: Locked endpoint changes and distributor removal previously left registered availability stale; unregister with a null endpoint could also skip invalidation.
findings.change: Receiver callbacks set registrationStatus to UNKNOWN and restart the network when a REGISTERED state is invalidated. Locked paths do not access endpoint/device/VAPID values. The unlocked unregister path invalidates state even when refreshEndpoint(null) would be a no-op.
findings.historical_runtime: PASS on API 30 for synthetic refresh-job missing-VAPID fallback on tree 24a27bf3ddf2f23593f5a11e3230b66b335bc2a3; predates this fix and does not validate locked callbacks.

findings.summary: Inherited endpoint-rotation bug: changing a registered endpoint could leave availability REGISTERED if MollySocket rejected the update. The callback now sets PENDING before enqueue; the existing IOException path sets UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: The same callback and failure behavior exists in the pinned Molly target (source-reviewed); this patch fixes that inherited behavior. No deployed/live MollySocket or HTTP retry timing was exercised.
findings.change: On changed non-null endpoint, REGISTERED is invalidated to PENDING before the refresh job is queued. The actual refresh-job callback test injects a specific IOException from the MollySocket repository boundary and verifies UNKNOWN, pushAvailable=false, and one registration attempt. Same-endpoint updates remain idempotent.

test_result.scope: 9 receiver security/availability tests (including actual endpoint callback + refresh job IOException path and same-endpoint idempotence) plus 16 URI validation tests; 25 total.
test_result.note: Focused run used identical test body before import-only ktlint formatting; official ktlint passed after formatting. Full staging suite remains pending.

findings.retry_limits: Refresh jobs remain capped at three attempts and six hours with at most two factory instances; retry cadence and live recovery are source-reviewed only.

findings.summary: The app receiver is exported without a signature permission; connector 3.0.10 gates callbacks on a stored registration token mapped to an instance, but does not authenticate the sender package.
findings.evidence: Compiled MessagingReceiver.onReceive bytecode retained in runtime/network-contracts/MessagingReceiverImpl.javap.txt and connector-classes.jar; Robolectric missing/unknown token cases passed in the focused receiver suite.

findings.summary: Locked push handling can post only a generic may-have-messages notice, guarded by the existing preference. It does not deserialize or display protected contents.
findings.evidence: UnifiedPushReceiver.onMessageLocked and FcmFetchManager.postMayHaveMessagesNotificationForLockedPush; Robolectric tests passed for urgent preference gating, malformed payload, and locked test payload. Payload classification is substring-based and can misclassify unexpected content.

findings.summary: Candidate DeviceAttributes serialization matches the five fields consumed by the examined dated Signal-Server linked-device request handler.
findings.evidence: DTO test output and server source snapshots in runtime/network-contracts; deployed server revision and live account registration remain unknown.

findings.summary: If linked-device registration succeeds but prekey loading fails before the new local device record is saved, an orphan remote linked device can remain.
findings.evidence: Source path in MollySocketRepository.createDevice and verifyNewDevice; no live provisioning/failure injection ran.

findings.summary: Discovery and registration disable redirects; exact OkHttp 5.3.2 loopback probe found no Basic Authorization header from URL userinfo and did not send fragments.
findings.evidence: runtime/network-contracts/userinfo-probe.json and userinfo-probe.log; ignored URL components remain low-severity parser hygiene.

findings.summary: Copying server parameters places device credentials and endpoint into clipboard through the sensitive clipboard helper; synthetic API 30 clipboard expiry was exercised.
findings.evidence: Historical API 30 run; API 33+ clipboard metadata remains untested.

limitations: The new receiver regression tests cover local callback and connector behavior; they do not exercise physical-device delivery.
No live Signal account, Signal service, MollySocket, or real UnifiedPush distributor was used.
Android 13+ clipboard metadata and physical-device notification behavior were not tested.
Historical API 30 runtime evidence belongs to tree 24a27bf3ddf2f23593f5a11e3230b66b335bc2a3, before the current source fix.

The callback tests model Signal UI passphrase locking; Signal KeyValueStore remains accessible. They do not model Molly encrypted database/master-secret locking or prove end-to-end lock hardening or protected-credential erasure.
